title: Unreasoned theft assessment set aside despite s.127 appeal
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Ashok Bhushan, J.; Vinay Kumar Mathur, J.
disposition: Assessment set aside; fresh order after considering reply.
headnote: Division Bench set aside a Rs.83.31 lakh theft assessment under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. An order that only refers to the consumer's reply without considering any ground is not a reasoned order. Availability of appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 did not bar writ interference on those facts. Licensee given liberty to pass a fresh order within four weeks after considering the reply; consumer to keep paying regular bills.
facts: M/s S.S. Ice and Cold Storage sought quashing of an Executive Engineer's 21 October 2011 assessment of Rs.83,31,462 after a 25 September 2011 checking of its cold storage. The unit had been inspected on 18 September 2011 and an MRI taken on 22 September 2011. A 29 September 2011 provisional notice assessed theft for 365 days under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner filed a 43-page reply on 10 October 2011. The final order referred to that reply but considered none of its grounds.

reusable_constructions.construction: Writ is not barred by section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 where the assessment is not a reasoned order because the assessing officer failed to consider any ground in the consumer's reply.

An assessment that merely recites that a reply was filed, without dealing with any of the grounds taken, is not a reasoned order and is liable to be set aside, with liberty to pass a fresh order after considering the reply.

holding_units.holding: Although an appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 lay against the theft assessment, the Court set aside the 21 October 2011 order because it was not a reasoned order: the assessing officer referred to the petitioner's 10 October 2011 reply but considered none of the grounds. The licensee was given liberty to pass a fresh order after considering the reply within four weeks of production of a certified copy. The petitioner was directed to continue paying regular bills as they fell due.

not_decided.point: Merits of the theft assessment, including the 365-day period and the MRI and regular-checking grounds
not_decided.note: Left to the assessing officer on a fresh order after considering the reply.
